subject: crs
topic: The baptism, temptation and call of the disciples

kept.q: In the first temptation in the wilderness, the devil challenged Jesus to turn stones into bread. With what scripture did Jesus reply to the devil?
options: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God
Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve
Get thee behind me, Satan
kept.explanation: Jesus quoted Deuteronomy to show that true life depends on obedience to God's word, not bread alone. This was His answer to the first temptation concerning hunger.

kept.q: After calling Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John, Jesus went further into Galilee and called a tax collector sitting at the tax office. Where was this tax collector sitting when Jesus called him?

kept.explanation: Matthew (Levi) was sitting at the receipt of custom, the place where taxes were collected, when Jesus called him to follow Him. He immediately left his work to become a disciple.

kept.q: A Sunday School teacher explains that when Jesus called His first four disciples by the Sea of Galilee, they responded in a particular manner that teaches Christians about discipleship today. Based on the Gospel account, how did Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John respond to the call?
options: They forsook their nets and family business and followed Him at once
They requested three days to consult their families first
They asked Jesus to first pay off their fishing debts
They followed Him only after He performed a miracle for them
kept.explanation: The Gospels record that the four fishermen left their nets and boats immediately to follow Jesus without delay or excuse. This prompt obedience is held up as a model of true discipleship.

kept.q: During the second temptation on the pinnacle of the temple, the devil quoted scripture to persuade Jesus to throw Himself down, claiming angels would bear Him up. How did Jesus respond to this misuse of scripture?
options: He said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
He said, Man shall not live by bread alone
He said, Get thee hence, Satan
He remained silent and walked away
kept.explanation: Jesus corrected the devil's twisting of scripture by quoting that one must not put the Lord God to the test. This shows Jesus countering every temptation with correct understanding of scripture.

q.q: John the Baptist preached a message to the Jews before the coming of Jesus. Which of the following best describes the central theme of his preaching?
options: A call to repentance and preparation for the coming kingdom
A call to pay tribute to Caesar without delay
A call to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem
A call to join the Roman army for protection
q.explanation: John the Baptist's preaching centred on repentance, telling the people to prepare the way for the Messiah. This is recorded in the Gospels before the baptism of Jesus.

q.q: A pastor in Ibadan teaches that the temptation of Jesus in the wilderness was not merely a personal test but had a deeper spiritual significance for believers today. What is the main lesson Christians draw from this event?
options: Believers can overcome temptation by relying on the word of God as Jesus did
Believers should avoid fasting since it exposes one to temptation
Believers must always seek a sign before obeying God
Believers should test God to confirm His promises
q.explanation: Jesus overcame every temptation by quoting scripture, showing believers that knowledge and use of God's word gives victory over temptation. This is the key moral lesson from the wilderness temptations.

q.q: Immediately after His baptism in the River Jordan, where was Jesus led before He began His temptation by the devil?
options: Into the wilderness
Into the temple at Jerusalem
Into the synagogue at Capernaum
Into the upper room
q.explanation: The Bible records that after His baptism, Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. This happened before He began His public ministry.

q.q: Considering the full account of Jesus' baptism and the three temptations that followed, what common lesson links both events for a candidate studying discipleship in Christian Religious Studies?
options: Divine approval at baptism was followed by a testing of obedience before public ministry began
Baptism guarantees a believer will never face temptation afterward
The temptations proved Jesus needed further purification after baptism
John the Baptist personally supervised the temptation process
q.explanation: At baptism, God publicly affirmed Jesus as His beloved Son, and immediately afterward Jesus was tested in the wilderness to prove His obedience and readiness for ministry. This sequence shows that divine calling is often followed by testing before service begins.
